title: internal TLS handshake prober terraform module for hybrid NLB/ALB ingress
creator: Asha Patel
description: Create a reusable Terraform module that deploys an internal hybrid load-balancer ingress for Private (VPC) deployments which performs active TLS handshake probing (SNI + cert validation) as the primary healthcheck and supports graceful TLS cert rotation and staged upgrades. This module must support NLB pass-through to backend TLS services as well as ALB TLS termination for routes that need application-layer routing. Provide configuration knobs for probe behavior, connection draining, and a canary rollout path.
acceptance_criteria: 1) Module deploys into a VPC with examples for both NLB pass-through and ALB termination. 2) Active TLS handshake prober validates SNI and leaf certificate CN/SAN for target groups and reports status via target group health. 3) Cert rotation flow demonstrated with zero-downtime listener swap in a blue/green canary. 4) Terraform examples and unit tests (terraform-compliance or terratest) exist in repo. 5) Monitoring dashboard link and runbook updated.
implementation_notes:
- Module will create two optional submodules: nlb_pass_through and alb_tls_termination.
- Health probe implemented as a small ECS Fargate task (or Lambda) that runs TCP+TLS handshake to target IP:port and asserts expected SNI and certificate thumbprint or SAN. Probe publishes status to CloudWatch custom metrics and an ALB/NLB target-group-compatible health endpoint (HTTP 200/503 shim).
- For NLB mode, the module adds a health-check target group backed by the prober; for ALB mode, use ALB health checks pointed at the probe shim on each target instance.
- Provide variables: probe_enabled, probe_interval, probe_timeout, probe_sni, probe_expected_cert_fingerprint, enable_canary, canary_weight, connection_draining_timeout, shutdown_grace_period.
- Support optional IAM role and KMS key for probe to fetch private certs when SNI validation requires intermediary CA chains.
- Integrate with existing terraform edge modules where possible to avoid duplication.
tests:
- Terratest integration that deploys module in a sandbox VPC, spins up a simple TLS-terminating backend (nginx with certs) and a TLS backend for NLB pass-through, verifies probe metrics, and simulates cert rotation.
- Unit plan tests for variable permutations (probe on/off, ALB/NLB).
- Chaos test: terminate a backend during canary rollout and ensure health checks failover to fallback pool.
- Add security test to ensure probe role cannot exfiltrate private keys (KMS access scoped).
runbook:
- How to trigger cert rotation: update cert_arn variable, enable canary, apply terraform. Monitor CloudWatch metric 'ingress/tls_probe_success_rate' and ALB target group health.
- If probe starts failing for new cert: verify probe_sni and expected fingerprint variables; check probe task logs in CloudWatch.
- To rollback: flip canary_weight to 0 and re-apply, or restore previous cert_arn.
- Escalation: tag on-call infra engineer and channel #infra-oper in Slack.
risk_assessment: Medium-high: modifying ingress and TLS rotation impacts all private customers. Major risks are probe false negatives (blocking healthy pods), IAM/KMS misconfigurations exposing keys, and accidental public exposure if listeners misconfigured. Mitigations include conservative default: probe disabled by default, canary enabled for rotation, automated plan checks in CI, and security review before GA.
rollback_plan: 1) Abort terraform apply if plan shows more than expected changes. 2) For cert-related failures, revert cert_arn and restore canary_weight to previous value. 3) If probe causes outage, set probe_enabled=false in module (module supports runtime toggle) and re-apply. 4) Re-enable probe only after root-cause identified.
